module priority_encoder #(
    parameter WIDTH = 4,
    parameter LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY = 0
)(
    input  wire [WIDTH-1:0] input_unencoded,
    output wire output_valid,
    output wire [$clog2(WIDTH)-1:0] output_encoded,
    output wire [WIDTH-1:0] output_unencoded
);

parameter LEVELS = WIDTH > 2 ? $clog2(WIDTH) : 1;
parameter W = 2**LEVELS;

generate
if (WIDTH == 128 && LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY == 0 && LEVELS == 7 && W == 128) begin : fast_msb128
    wire [15:0] group_valid;
    wire [15:0] group_enable;
    wire [15:0] group_winner;
    wire [15:0] encoded_terms [6:0];
    genvar g, j, k;

    for (g = 0; g < 16; g = g + 1) begin : groups
        wire [7:0] x;
        wire [7:0] local_winner;
        wire [2:0] local_code;
        assign x = input_unencoded[g*8 +: 8];
        assign group_valid[g] = |x;
        if (g == 15) begin : top_group
            assign group_enable[g] = 1'b1;
        end else begin : other_group
            assign group_enable[g] = ~(|group_valid[15:g+1]);
        end
        assign group_winner[g] = group_valid[g] & group_enable[g];

        for (j = 0; j < 8; j = j + 1) begin : bits_in_group
            if (j == 7) begin : highest
                assign local_winner[j] = x[j];
            end else begin : lower
                assign local_winner[j] = x[j] & ~(|x[7:j+1]);
            end
            if (g == 0 && j == 0) begin : zero_default
                assign output_unencoded[g*8+j] = group_enable[g] & ~(|x[7:1]);
            end else begin : ordinary_output
                assign output_unencoded[g*8+j] = group_enable[g] & local_winner[j];
            end
        end

        assign local_code[2] = |x[7:4];
        assign local_code[1] = (|x[7:6]) | ((~(|x[7:4])) & (|x[3:2]));
        assign local_code[0] = local_winner[7] | local_winner[5] |
                               local_winner[3] | local_winner[1];

        for (k = 0; k < 3; k = k + 1) begin : low_code
            assign encoded_terms[k][g] = group_enable[g] & local_code[k];
        end
        for (k = 3; k < 7; k = k + 1) begin : high_code
            if ((g & (1 << (k-3))) != 0) begin : contributes
                assign encoded_terms[k][g] = group_winner[g];
            end else begin : no_contribution
                assign encoded_terms[k][g] = 1'b0;
            end
        end
    end

    for (k = 0; k < 7; k = k + 1) begin : encoded_outputs
        assign output_encoded[k] = |encoded_terms[k];
    end
    assign output_valid = |group_valid;
end else begin : reference_parameters
    wire [W-1:0] input_padded;
    wire [W/2-1:0] stage_valid [LEVELS-1:0];
    wire [W/2-1:0] stage_enc [LEVELS-1:0];
    assign input_padded = {{W-WIDTH{1'b0}}, input_unencoded};
    genvar l, n;

    for (n = 0; n < W/2; n = n + 1) begin : loop_in
        assign stage_valid[0][n] = |input_padded[n*2+1:n*2];
        if (LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin : lsb
            assign stage_enc[0][n] = !input_padded[n*2];
        end else begin : msb
            assign stage_enc[0][n] = input_padded[n*2+1];
        end
    end
    for (l = 1; l < LEVELS; l = l + 1) begin : loop_levels
        for (n = 0; n < W/(2*2**l); n = n + 1) begin : loop_compress
            assign stage_valid[l][n] = |stage_valid[l-1][n*2+1:n*2];
            if (LSB_HIGH_PRIORITY) begin : lsb
                assign stage_enc[l][(n+1)*(l+1)-1:n*(l+1)] =
                    stage_valid[l-1][n*2] ?
                    {1'b0, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+1)*l-1:(n*2)*l]} :
                    {1'b1, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+2)*l-1:(n*2+1)*l]};
            end else begin : msb
                assign stage_enc[l][(n+1)*(l+1)-1:n*(l+1)] =
                    stage_valid[l-1][n*2+1] ?
                    {1'b1, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+2)*l-1:(n*2+1)*l]} :
                    {1'b0, stage_enc[l-1][(n*2+1)*l-1:(n*2)*l]};
            end
        end
    end
    assign output_valid = stage_valid[LEVELS-1];
    assign output_encoded = stage_enc[LEVELS-1];
    assign output_unencoded = 1 << output_encoded;
end
endgenerate
endmodule

`default_nettype wire
",
  "bottleneck": "The baseline critical paths terminate at output_unencoded after traversing priority selection, an encoded-index mux network, and binary-to-one-hot decoding. The reported high-drive mux stage alone contributes 0.57 ns and also feeds downstream decode logic.",
  "rewrite": "Specialize the fixed 128-bit MSB-priority configuration into sixteen parallel eight-bit groups. Compute local winners concurrently with group-valid reductions and higher-group exclusion masks. Drive one-hot outputs directly from local winners and group enables, bypassing binary encoding and subsequent decoding. Compute the binary index separately using parallel local encoders and masked OR reductions. Retain the reference implementation for other parameter configurations, including overrides of LEVELS and W.",
  "expected_timing_gain": "The direct one-hot path removes the serial encode-then-decode dependency responsible for the reported critical paths. A reduction from the 2.23 ns baseline is expected, but no numerical timing gain or passing STA result is claimed without running the specified mapping and constraints. The lower encoded-index bits and group-enable fanout are likely new timing limits.",
  "area_or_other_cost": "Adds explicit local winner logic and group-selection masks while removing the specialized configuration's general encoded-index decoder and mux tree. The structure is intended to fit below the 4694.627520 um2 cap, but mapped area and electrical compliance remain unmeasured. Group-enable nets drive local outputs and encoding terms, so synthesis may insert buffers or increase cell drive strengths.",
  "functional_boundaries": "Purely combinational with unchanged ports, parameter declarations, and priority. For the fixed configuration, every nonzero input selects its highest asserted bit. For an all-zero input, output_valid is zero, output_encoded is zero, and output_unencoded is 128'b1, preserving the reference's nonzero one-hot default. Other configurations retain the reference logic, including padding, truncation, and LSB-priority zero-input behavior. No state, latency, assumptions, assertions, undefined outputs, or external helper modules are introduced."
}
